solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Barnum & Bailey's first and last autumn production

indicators.note: first here takes the opening stretch of the circus founder's surname, its first three letters
last here takes the closing stretch of the partner's surname, its final three letters

explanation.surface: A circus programme note about the opening and closing acts of Barnum & Bailey's autumn show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' and 'last' take three letters each here, BAR from Barnum and LEY from Bailey, though the clue does not say how many; the surface's circus 'production' is really a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal crop is harvested in late summer and autumn, so it is a product of the season's harvest.

clue.text: Director quits bankrupt Leeds tour firm

indicators.note: bankrupt means broken, so the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled
quits says the director leaves, so that letter is removed from the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A Leeds travel company goes bust and one of its directors walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bankrupt' scrambles LEEDS TOUR, and 'quits' removes the D for Director from those letters, leaving eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being steadfast and unwavering in purpose is a standard synonym, as in a firm or determined stance.

clue.text: I study diplomacy, said to be vital in interview

indicators.note: said to be marks the first word as spoken, so its sound is written as a homophone

parts.note: the pronoun I is spoken exactly like the organ of sight
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
tact is the skill of handling people diplomatically

explanation.surface: A candidate claims that studying diplomacy is vital in an interview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' turns I into its sound-alike EYE; CON means study, as in conning a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Interview advice stresses meeting the interviewer's gaze, so looking someone in the eye is essential there.

clue.text: It transmits live north and south

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for live is read going both ways, once downwards and once upwards

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A transmitter broadcasting live programmes to both the north and the south.
explanation.walkthrough: BE (live) is written once going south (downwards) and once going north (upwards), so it reads the same either way. The Beeb is the nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for the British Broadcasting Corporation, which transmits radio and television programmes.

clue.text: Inner membrane closed in another part of body

indicators.note: in places the word for closed inside the name of a body region

parts.note: the perineum is the area between the anus and the genitals
to, as in a door pushed to, means closed

explanation.surface: Anatomy lesson: an inner membrane closed off inside a further part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: TO means closed, as in 'pull the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: This serous lining coats the abdominal cavity and its organs, a membrane deep inside the body.

clue.text: Oz guy almost picked up check

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, so the letters read from the bottom upwards
almost means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Bruce is the stock name for an Australian man

explanation.surface: An Australian bloke nearly picked up a cheque, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BRUCE, the stereotypical Aussie name, to BRUC, and 'picked up' turns that upwards; 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain or hold back something is a direct synonym, as in reining in spending.

clue.text: Fruit machine's played with these in fact

definitions.text: Fruit machine's played with these in fact

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are played around with, rearranged so the phrase splits into two

parts.note: the two words are taken letter for letter as the fodder pool, the possessive ending adding no letter

explanation.surface: A one-armed bandit is, literally, operated using these arm bones.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FRUIT MACHINE, rearranged ('played'), give the answer plus IN FACT. Old fruit machines, or one-armed bandits, were worked by pulling a lever with the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: These upper-arm bones power the pull of the lever on a one-armed bandit.

clue.text: Bachelor and writer go thieving

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A single man and an author turn to stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery by gangs of outlaws; the noun names the activity of thieving.

clue.text: With this girl welded energetically

indicators.note: welded suggests the letters are fused and reshaped, so the girl's letters join the answer's to form the last word

explanation.surface: A young woman doing vigorous welding work with a gas torch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters plus GIRL rearrange to ENERGETICALLY ('welded'), and the whole clue describes the gas.
explanation.definitionFit: This fuel gas burns with oxygen in the hot flame of an oxy-fuel welding torch.

clue.text: It's of limited value wiggling round middle of mouth

definitions.text: It's of limited value wiggling round middle of mouth

indicators.note: round says the scrambled letters go around the central letter
wiggling stirs the shortened letters about
limited means the word is cut short, losing its last letter
middle of takes the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something of little use wobbling about in the middle of the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims VALUE to VALU, 'wiggling' rearranges that to UVLA, and 'round' wraps it around U, the centre of 'mouth'. The whole clue describes the dangling flap.
explanation.definitionFit: This small fleshy lobe hangs at the back of the soft palate and has little obvious function.

clue.text: Number One's back in swimming club? It's a pride issue

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the anagram
swimming suggests the letters float about and rearrange
back reverses the number and the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A club captain returns to the swimming club; is that about pride?
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges CLUB and 'back' turns the pair round before 'in' puts them inside. A pride is a group of lions, and an issue is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of big cats, and issue means offspring, so the youngster born into it fits.

clue.text: What some isolated families do at home about sleeping?

indicators.note: at home means sitting inside, so the word for about is housed within the phrase for sleeping

parts.note: someone sleeping is in bed
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A question about the bedtime habits of families living in remote places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' sets RE inside IN BED; it looks like IN, but works as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Families cut off from others may mate within a close kin group, producing offspring from related parents.

clue.text: Second person's share of carry-out

indicators.note: share of means only a portion of the compound word's letters is taken

explanation.surface: Someone's portion of a takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A carry-out is a takeaway meal in Scotland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the addressee's pronoun the second person, the one being spoken to.

clue.text: Yes man in Ayr sadly not in a top group of celebs?

indicators.note: sadly signals that the three short words are in a sorry, jumbled state

parts.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A man in Ayr who says yes is sadly not among the elite celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town in Scotland; 'Yes' was the pro-independence side in Scotland's 2014 referendum, so a Yes man there is a separatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigners for Scottish independence voted Yes in the 2014 referendum, so a Yes voter in Scotland favours self-rule.

clue.text: Rent up, New Yorker avoids capitals for job at home

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for rent is read from the bottom

parts.note: to let is to rent out

indicators.note: avoids capitals drops the capital letters that begin each of the two words

explanation.surface: Rents rise, so a New Yorker shuns big cities in favour of working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LET to TEL; 'avoids capitals' takes away the initial N and Y of New Yorker, leaving EWORKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works from home via phone and internet; the definition describes them by their remote employment.

clue.text: Made less time for news due at ground

parts.note: News at Ten is the long-running ITV evening news bulletin, so its time is at ten

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Time was cut back because news fell due at the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a British evening TV news programme, giving AT TEN; 'ground' rearranges DUE AT to UATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakened or reduced in force, thinned out, so diminished or lessened.

clue.text: McCartney left out old Stone

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped from the first name

parts.note: Stella McCartney is the fashion designer, daughter of Paul

explanation.surface: A Beatle omitted an old Rolling Stone from the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'McCartney' suggests Paul, but it is Stella the designer; 'old Stone' suggests a Rolling Stone, but it is an ancient carved slab.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright slab of carved or inscribed rock was set up in ancient times as a monument.

clue.text: Irishman recruits a boy randomly for plant

indicators.note: recruits means the man takes the others in, enclosing them

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name

indicators.note: randomly means the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: An Irish employer hires a lad at random to work at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' scrambles A BOY and 'recruits' puts the result inside the name. 'plant' looks like a factory but is the legume.
explanation.definitionFit: This legume is grown widely for its edible seeds and oil, a crop and so a growing thing.

clue.text: Invention that helps Rory

definitions.meaning: an invention can be a made-up story, a falsehood
golfer Rory McIlroy is helped by a good position of the ball on the course

explanation.surface: A gadget that assists a man named Rory.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory McIlroy is a leading golfer; a ball's position on the ground is its lie, and a good one helps the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabrication is something invented, and in golf the ball's resting position is its lie.

clue.text: The way to block river with a smack?

indicators.note: to block means the abbreviation for a road sits inside the river, blocking it

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A question about blocking a river by sinking a fishing boat in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is a river in Scotland. A smack is a fishing boat, but it also means a flavour, as in 'a smack of garlic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a taste or flavour, so something with plenty of it is full of flavour.

clue.text: Small rulers nicked as well as waste

indicators.note: nicked means cut into, so the joining word goes between the two royal abbreviations

parts.note: QU and ER are both abbreviations for a queen, a ruler
and means as well as

explanation.surface: Little rulers got stolen, and something was wasted too.
explanation.walkthrough: The rulers are two queens, by their abbreviations Queen and Elizabeth Regina; 'nicked' cuts the joining word in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away or use extravagantly is a direct synonym, as in squandering an inheritance.

clue.text: MacArthur, say, months away at sea, rounds Cape

indicators.note: rounds means the scrambled letters go around the abbreviation for the headland
at sea means in confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Ellen MacArthur spends months away at sea and sails round a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Ellen MacArthur is a British record-breaking solo sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen MacArthur is an example of a female sailor, famous for a fast solo round-the-world voyage.

clue.text: Bottomless caldera melted the young rock there

indicators.note: melted means the remaining letters run together and reshape
bottomless in a down entry means the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A geology scene: a bottomless volcanic crater with molten young rock in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottomless' drops the final A of CALDERA, and 'melted' rearranges CALDER. 'Young rock' suggests new lava, but babies are rocked in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies are rocked to sleep in a crib, so a little one is gently swung in it.

clue.text: Even Muslims seen in minster here?

indicators.note: even picks the letters in even-numbered positions: second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Even Muslim visitors may be seen inside a Christian cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The German city of Ulm has a minster with the world's tallest church spire.
explanation.definitionFit: This German city on the Danube is home to a famous Gothic church, the tallest in the world.

clue.text: Change amount cattle regularly cropped

indicators.note: regularly cropped means every other letter is cut away, keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A farmer changes the number of cattle, with pasture grazed at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter in form or nature, a synonym used especially of genes and organisms.

clue.text: Barbecue lamb rump and more nuts, wasting carbon

indicators.note: rump is the hind end, so the last letter of the word is taken
wasting means losing the element's symbol from the word

parts.note: crazier means more nuts, more mad
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A barbecue menu: lamb rump and extra nuts, with the charcoal burning away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rump' takes the end of 'lamb', B; 'wasting' strips C from CRAZIER.
explanation.definitionFit: This open metal stand holds burning coals, and food can be grilled over it outdoors.

clue.text: Trendy Poles bar experts from them

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Fashionable Poles ban specialists from their bars.
explanation.walkthrough: In England, barristers ('bar experts') are called to the Bar through the Inns of Court, so they come from them.
explanation.definitionFit: The four Inns of Court in London admit and train barristers, the professionals at the Bar.

clue.text: Con wins at fencing

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the short word wraps around the word for wins

parts.note: gains means wins or obtains

explanation.surface: A cheat wins at a fencing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle or a convict, but it is the opposite of pro.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros and cons are arguments for and opposed; a con is a point in opposition.

clue.text: It's at bomb's core

indicators.note: core takes the centre of the word, its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A statement about what sits at the heart of a nuclear weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes splitting the nucleus at the heart of an atomic weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear weapons work by splitting the nuclei of these basic particles of matter, so they lie at its heart.

clue.text: Ready to drop unrestricted visiting

definitions.meaning: someone ready to drop is exhausted, worn out
unrestricted means with no limits, like a form of wrestling where any hold is allowed

explanation.surface: Visiting with no limits until one is ready to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: All-in wrestling is a British term for wrestling with almost no rules.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exhausted, and also comprehensive or without restriction, as in an all-inclusive price.

clue.text: Flight operator got in touch

indicators.note: got in means the abbreviation is taken inside the word for touch

parts.note: a touch of something is an element of it

explanation.surface: An airline operator made contact about a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' looks like air travel, but it means running away to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off secretly to marry is a flight from home, an escape with a lover.
